nodes.name: FeMoO4 solvothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 1 mmol FeCl2·4H2O was taken in a 100 ml round-bottom flask and dissolved in 10 mL of water-ethylene glycol mixture (1:1) with constant stirring using a magnetic stirrer, and then 1 mmol Na2MoO4·2H2O was added to the stirred precursor solution. The solution was kept stirring for further 1 h, and the resultant mixture was transferred to a 25 mL Teflon reactor and put inside a stainless-steel autoclave at 180°C for 12 h. After normal cooling of the autoclave, the sample was washed with water and ethanol through ultracentrifugation. The washed sample was then dried at 60°C for 2 h in an air oven, and the sample was ground well with an agate mortar for further characterization.

nodes.name: α-FeO(OH) precipitation
nodes.procedure: Ferric nitrate [Fe(NO3)3·xH2O, 48.4 mg] was dissolved into 7 mL of Milli-Q water in a 20 mL vial with continuous stirring using a magnetic stirrer. The pH of the solution was then adjusted to ~pH 12 with the dropwise addition of 0.5 mL of 1 M KOH. After that, the volume was adjusted to 10 mL by the addition of Milli-Q water. The cloudy orange mixture was continuously stirred for 24 h at room temperature. After 24 h, the solution was washed with water and ethanol several times through centrifugation to get pure α-FeO(OH).

nodes.name: γ-FeO(OH) precipitation
nodes.procedure: For the synthesis of γ-FeO(OH), ferrous sulfate (FeSO4·7H2O, 50 mg) was dissolved into 7 mL of Milli-Q water in a 20 mL vial with continuous stirring using a magnetic stirrer. Then, 2.1 mL of 0.2 M NaOH solution was added, which leads to the color change from light-yellow to orange and finally cloudy orange. The volume of the solution was adjusted to 10 mL by the addition of the solvent. The resultant solution was continuously stirred for 24 h at room temperature. After 24 h, the solution was washed by water and ethanol several times through centrifugation to get pure γ-FeO(OH).

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD confirms monoclinic α-FeMoO4 phase (JCPDS 22-0628, space group P2/m) with sharp intense diffractions; crystallite size ~58 nm from Debye-Scherrer on (-220) reflection.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of sharp and intense diffractions confirmed the crystalline nature of the as-synthesized FeMoO4. The diffraction peaks can be indexed with the standard diffraction pattern of monoclinic FeMoO4 (JCPDS 22-0628)... Implication of the Debye-Scherrer's equation on the major reflection (-220) provided an average crystallite size (calculated) of ca. 58 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: FESEM shows nanoscopic FeMoO4 particles with irregular shapes and some aggregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of the synthesized FeMoO4 powder material was analyzed by field emission scanning electron microscopic (FESEM) imaging. Nanoscopic feature with irregular shapes were visible in the FESEM images (Figures 2a, S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX confirms Fe:Mo atomic ratio of 1:1 and homogeneous distribution of Fe, Mo, and O elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectrum recorded from a large area inferred the presence of Fe and Mo in a 1:1 atomic ratio (Figure S4). The homogeneous distribution of Fe, Mo, and O in the FeMoO4 powder material was confirmed by SEM-EDX elemental mapping (Figure 2b-e).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals nanoparticles with rough edges; HRTEM shows (220) lattice fringes d=0.34 nm confirming monoclinic FeMoO4; SAED shows polycrystalline diffraction rings for (220), (400), (-110) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of a single nanoparticle exhibited well-resolved atomic fringes for the (d220) Bragg's planes with an interplanar d-spacing of 0.34 nm confirming further the monoclinic FeMoO4 phase (Figure 2g). However, the polycrystalline nature of FeMoO4 was evident from the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern where diffraction rings for (220), (400), and (-110) were indexed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman bands at 347, 778, 870, 923, and 960 cm⁻¹ correspond to MoO4 stretching and bending modes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FeMoO4 possesses Raman-allowed characteristic vibrations, and the bands were observed at Raman shift values of 347, 778, 870, 923, and 960 cm⁻¹ (Figure 3a). The bands at 923 and 960 cm⁻¹ correspond to the symmetric Raman-allowed stretching vibrations of the distorted [MoO4] unit.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR bands at 915 and 760 cm⁻¹ correspond to symmetric and asymmetric stretching of Mo=O bond.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectrum of FeMoO4, several intense bands were observed (Figure 3b). The bands positioned at 915 and 760 cm⁻¹ correspond to the symmetric and asymmetric stretching, respectively, for the M=O bond present in the MoO4 unit.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe 2p3/2 at 710.4 eV and 713.2 eV (higher oxidation state), Mo 3d5/2 at 232.8 eV (MoVI), O 1s at 530.6 eV (oxide).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution core level Fe 2p scan provided binding energy values for two spin-orbit components Fe2p3/2 and Fe2p1/2 at 710.4 and 723.7 eV, respectively... The core level Mo 3d spectrum showed two prominent peaks at 232.8 eV and 235.9 eV for the spin orbit components Mo3d5/2 and Mo3d3/2, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER PXRD shows broad diffractions indicating amorphous nature with weak reflections indexed to polycrystalline α-FeO(OH) (JCPDS 29-0713).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Broad diffraction of the PXRD data primarily indicated the small/amorphous nature of the isolated particles. Indexing of the weak reflections with reference to JCPDS data (29-0713) for α-FeO(OH) indicated the formation of polycrystalline α-FeO(OH) from the FeMoO4 precatalyst (Figure 7a).

nodes.characterization_summary: Quasi in situ Raman after CV cycles shows disappearance of Mo-O bands and appearance of ferrihydrite bands (625-800 cm⁻¹, 247, 373, 521 cm⁻¹); after CA-OER shows α-FeO(OH) bands at 289, 392, 597 cm⁻¹ with residual ferrihydrite.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After exposure of the FeMoO4/NF followed by 10 CV cycles, the characteristic Mo-O Raman bands between 750 and 1000 cm⁻¹ completely disappeared, whereas a broad band over 625-800 cm⁻¹ appeared... With the progress of CA-OER from 2-12 h, under quasi in situ conditions, Raman data were recorded with the WE. The intensity of the broad band for the ferrihydrite slowly diminished, whereas an intense band at 289 cm⁻¹ along with 392 and 597 cm⁻¹ indicated the evolution of the α FeO(OH) phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER XPS shows increased FeIII (Fe 2p3/2 at 710.9 eV), reduced Mo signal, O 1s peaks at 530.1 eV (lattice oxide), 531.3 eV (OH⁻), 534.6 eV (adsorbed water) confirming FeO(OH) formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The core level deconvoluted Fe 2p spectrum showed a higher percentage of FeIII as confirmed from the spin orbit component of Fe 2p3/2 and Fe 2p1/2 at 710.9 and 725.2 eV, respectively... A peak broadening of the O 1s core-level spectrum along with its deconvolution peaks to three binding energy values of 530.1, 531.3, and 534.6 eV correspond to lattice oxide (O2-), hydroxylated oxygen (OH-), and surface adsorbed water species, respectively.
